author: jvm
cardQuote: Not to mention no product since it duplicates the 'share on twitter' functionality of the camera app. In 2 years, nobody will remember what instagram was.
quote: Not to mention no product since it duplicates the 'share on twitter' functionality of the camera app. In 2 years, nobody will remember what instagram was.
outcome: Acquired for $1B; grew to 2B+ monthly users.
outcomeDetail: Facebook bought Instagram for $1 billion in 2012, when it had roughly 30 million users. Instagram became one of Meta's core apps, passed 2 billion monthly active users, and helped define the company's mobile advertising business.
note: The comment reduced Instagram to a duplicated camera feature. It became the photo layer of the world's largest social network.

author: ipaddr
cardQuote: This reminds me of google+. RIP threads - 2023-2023 Twitter may die but this will not replace it.
quote: This reminds me of google+. RIP threads - 2023-2023 Twitter may die but this will not replace it.
outcome: 100M signups in five days; 500M monthly users by 2026.
outcomeDetail: Threads launched on July 5, 2023 and became the fastest-growing consumer app in history, passing 100 million signups in five days. By mid-2026 Meta reported over 500 million monthly active users.
note: The 'RIP threads - 2023-2023' joke was stale within a week. Threads did not kill Twitter outright, but it became one of the largest text-based social apps.

author: tayo42
cardQuote: all of these networks are on the decline. rehashing something old seems like its doomed to fail.
quote: Do people actually want even more social media in their lives? I get the feeling Instagram is a enough. then chat apps do the rest. all of these networks are on the decline. rehashing something old seems like its doomed to fail.
outcome: 38M+ registered users by August 2025; a leading X alternative.
outcomeDetail: Bluesky grew from an invite-only beta to 30 million registered users by January 2025 and more than 38 million by August 2025. It became a major destination during the post-2024-election exodus from X.
note: The claim that social media was declining and a new network was 'doomed to fail' missed the appetite for a Twitter alternative. Bluesky's growth was uneven, but it reached tens of millions of users.

author: nwh
cardQuote: $3.5B for an app lots of developers could create over the weekend is absolutely incredible. It also has absolutely no income, and very little avenue for actually gaining any.
quote: $3.5B for an app lots of developers could create over the weekend is absolutely incredible. It also has absolutely no income, and very little avenue for actually gaining any. I don't know what they're doing to need seed money, I can only imagine that the service runs itself outside of tweaking EC2 instance sizes.
storyTitle: Snapchat Is Mulling Another Huge Round at a $3.5 Billion Valuation
outcome: IPO in 2017; 400M+ daily users and billions in ad revenue.
outcomeDetail: Snapchat IPO'd in 2017 at a $24 billion valuation and built a large advertising business. It reported more than 400 million daily active users and over $4 billion in annual revenue.
note: The 'no income' critique was fair in 2013 but wrong about the trajectory. Snapchat turned ephemeral messaging into a durable ad business.

author: staunch
cardQuote: Twitch is not going to be another YouTube success story. There just aren't enough great uses for live streaming yet and video game streaming is very far from being mainstream.
quote: Twitch is not going to be another YouTube success story. There just aren't enough great uses for live streaming yet and video game streaming is very far from being mainstream. Twitch obviously can't believe it's very close to reaching NFL-like status either or it wouldn't sell for a mere billion and change. Amazon or Google will piss off or drive away the Twitch user base. The users will all move to Hitbox.tv or any number of new sites that will pop up. It's easy to do live streaming, it's just expensive. This acquisition will bring funding and Yahoo will buy the next popular live streaming site.
outcome: Amazon paid ~$970M; Twitch remains the leading game-streaming platform.
outcomeDetail: Amazon bought Twitch in 2014 for about $970 million. Twitch stayed the dominant live-streaming site for games and a major subscriptions and advertising business, despite competition from YouTube and Mixer.
note: The prediction that users would flee to Hitbox and that game streaming was far from mainstream was wrong. Twitch became the category's default platform.

author: senectus1
cardQuote: it's even more ephemeral than twitter. there is no "community" behind it.. its purely entertainment. It'll die off. it has nothing to build on.
quote: pfft. its carefully targeted to children and the young. it's even more ephemeral than twitter. there is no "community" behind it.. its purely entertainment. It'll die off. it has nothing to build on.
outcome: 1B+ monthly users; one of the world's most-used apps.
outcomeDetail: TikTok passed 1 billion monthly active users and became a global cultural and advertising force. Its scale also made it a target of US ban legislation.
note: The 'purely entertainment, nothing to build on' take underestimated the recommendation feed and creator economy. TikTok did not die off; it became the template competitors copied.

author: orliesaurus
cardQuote: With the Netflix for videogames approach Discord enters another unsustainable model, with the first one being unlimited chat and voice-chat for everyone.
quote: I have been using Discord since the very beginning, as a replacement for TeamSpeak, Ventrilo and the occasional Mumble ( friends and onlinr friends). Also it replaced entirely Skype. And IRC for pugs and finding opponents to "fight". Discord is great and free. I would have never expected them to try and take a bite off Steam. Steam has a lot of issues but it's also the king of the hill and will be extremely hard to take a seizable chunk of their cake away. With the Netflix for videogames approach Discord enters another unsustainable model, with the first one being unlimited chat and voice-chat for everyone. I wish them the best, it would suck if Discord disappeared, but they're throwing a lot stones into the gaming well. And we all know how the gaming world is...
outcomeDetail: Discord's free chat and voice product kept growing well beyond gaming, and the company was valued at $15 billion in 2021. It reported more than 200 million monthly active users.
note: The comment was right that Discord's game store was a stretch, but wrong that free unlimited chat and voice was unsustainable. Those free features were the growth engine.

author: adventured
cardQuote: Just because users connect, doesn't mean you have a pot of gold.
quote: I'm trying to find an explanation for how WhatsApp's network is supposedly worth drastically more than Gmail / Yahoo / Hotmail webmail is. Just because users connect, doesn't mean you have a pot of gold. I believe this is a critical, flawed assumption that is being nearly universally made. Last generation's instant messaging apps were nearly worthless monetarily, and are still nearly worthless even today with tons of users. Why the assumption that today's mobile versions of instant messaging will be worth ... over a hundred billion dollars (apparently)? I've got an alternate theory. Today's WhatsApps and Snapchats will turn out to be terrible businesses, that aren't worth anywhere near what's being speculated. Today's user (mobile based) obsession will be viewed as not all that different from yesterday's eyeballs (web based) obsession. What are the consequences of that scenario?
storyTitle: Numbers That Explain Why Facebook Acquired WhatsApp
outcome: 2B+ users; acquired for $19B and became core to Meta.
outcomeDetail: Facebook bought WhatsApp for $19 billion in 2014. WhatsApp passed 2 billion users and became Meta's most widely used messaging app, even though direct monetization stayed limited.
note: The 'no pot of gold' analysis was wrong about strategic value. WhatsApp's scale and messaging graph became central to Meta's international strategy.

author: Freeboots
cardQuote: 2b messages is not cheap, where is their revenue if not from subscribers or from selling data? My only guess is that they are planning to charge for their api when they hit scale.
quote: +1, 2b messages is not cheap, where is their revenue if not from subscribers or from selling data? My only guess is that they are planning to charge for their api when they hit scale.
outcomeDetail: Telegram kept its free core, added Premium subscriptions and advertising, and reached 1 billion monthly active users. Pavel Durov said the company became profitable in 2024.
note: The prediction that Telegram would have to charge for its API missed the subscription-and-ads model. The free messaging layer remained the growth engine.

author: BitwiseFool
cardQuote: I assume they will end up like Tumblr after it went Safe for Work. Still around but nowhere near as popular and a shell of its former self.
quote: I assume they will end up like Tumblr after it went Safe for Work. Still around but nowhere near as popular and a shell of its former self.
storyTitle: OnlyFans to block sexually explicit videos starting in October
outcome: Ban reversed in six days; revenue reached $1.3B.
outcomeDetail: OnlyFans reversed the explicit-content ban six days later after creator backlash. The company kept growing, reporting about $1.3 billion in revenue in the year to November 2023 and 220 million registered consumers.
note: The Tumblr comparison assumed the ban would stick. OnlyFans backed down almost immediately, and the episode became a case study in creator power.

author: TD-Linux
cardQuote: I installed Yik Yak to see what all the hype was about, and discovered that it was substantially less insightful than 4chan's /b/ board.
quote: I installed Yik Yak to see what all the hype was about, and discovered that it was substantially less insightful than 4chan's /b/ board.
storyTitle: The inside story of Yik Yak
outcome: Shut down in 2017; its 2021 relaunch never regained scale.
outcomeDetail: Yik Yak shut down in 2017 after losing users and facing moderation problems. A 2021 relaunch was acquired by Sidechat in 2023 and never regained its original scale.
note: The 4chan comparison captured the app's core weakness: anonymous local posting without a durable community. Yik Yak never built one.

author: a3d6g2f7
cardQuote: Bad PR all around for the FB. FB, the business, is doomed. They already knew that. They just didn't tell you, the investor.
quote: Well, there's another article from Blodget on this fiasco that will soon hit the front page here. The NASDAQ snafu is one thing. A class action suit has been filed. But there has also been a class action suit against FB, alleging securities fraud. We don't have all the facts yet, but what we've got so far is enough to demand to know more. I think a court will agree. Bad PR all around for the FB. FB, the business, is doomed. They already knew that. They just didn't tell you, the investor. Maybe we should demand an ad-free FB. Advertisers are going to be pulling out anyway. And without ads, they could give us more privacy. Poetic justice. Where's that Like button?
storyTitle: Hedge Funder Who Bet $100 Million On Facebook IPO Is Furious
outcomeDetail: Facebook recovered from its messy IPO and grew into a trillion-dollar company with roughly 3 billion monthly users across its apps. Advertising remained one of the most profitable businesses in tech.
note: The 'FB, the business, is doomed' call was made during a bad IPO week, not a product collapse. Facebook's ad machine and mobile transition proved far more durable.

author: smsm42
cardQuote: I've never once encountered anybody linking to a post on Mastodon, and I am a voracious consumer of content.
quote: Being "better than Twitter" is not hard - Twitter is awful on almost any metric you can find. The only redeeming feature is has is that sometimes interesting people post interesting things there. Do they do it on Mastodon? I honestly have no idea - I've never once encountered anybody linking to a post on Mastodon, and I am a voracious consumer of content.
storyTitle: Mastodon Is Better Than Twitter: Elevator Pitch
outcome: 10M+ registered users; largest federated social network.
outcomeDetail: Mastodon grew from a niche network into the largest ActivityPub platform, passing 10 million registered accounts in March 2023 and about 2 million monthly active users. Major news organizations and governments set up instances.
note: The 'never encountered anybody linking to Mastodon' line did not survive the 2022 Twitter exodus. Mastodon did not replace Twitter, but it became the durable alternative in the fediverse.

author: miguelrochefort
cardQuote: I smell a bubble. They're not nearly worth any of this. Their service is trivial, and can't scale.
quote: I smell a bubble. They're not nearly worth any of this. Their service is trivial, and can't scale. They have a great user base, but I can't imagine them moving in the right direction. At the moment, it looks like a glorified wishlist. At one point, the paradox of choice will kick in, and they'll realize that too much (without proper curation) is as bad as not enough. I hope they will do the right thing (it's quite obvious what they should do), but I predict that they won't. They'll miss the big picture, focus on scaling in quantity (not quality), and burn through their money in no time. That's what happen to startups that think they have won. But that's just my prediction. We will see what will happen.
storyTitle: Pinterest Raises $225 Million at $3.8 Billion Valuation
outcomeDetail: Pinterest went public in 2019 and grew into a large visual-discovery and shopping platform with more than 500 million monthly active users. It built a substantial advertising business around purchase intent.
note: The 'glorified wishlist' critique missed the commercial intent behind the pins. Pinterest turned that intent into a durable ad business.

author: downandout
cardQuote: Twitter is better suited as a feature, not a product, and definitely not an $18 billion company.
quote: The comparison to Instagram is interesting. I used to do some marketing on Vine. Our traffic from Vine dropped more than 90% in less than 1 week after Instagram introduced video. That's how fast a replacement for Twitter could gobble up its business as well. IMO, Twitter is better suited as a feature, not a product, and definitely not an $18 billion company.
storyTitle: Twitter Prices IPO Above Estimates at $26 Per Share, Valuation Up to $18B
outcome: IPO in 2013; sold to Elon Musk for $44B in 2022.
outcomeDetail: Twitter IPO'd in 2013 and eventually became profitable before Elon Musk bought it for $44 billion in 2022. It remained a central real-time network for news and public argument, even as its ad business struggled.
note: The 'feature, not a product' call underestimated the network's staying power. Twitter outlived MySpace comparisons and became a $44 billion acquisition.
